title: A Second Life for a Winter Coat
title_ja: 冬のコートの第二の人生

source_links.title: UNEP: Sustainability and Circularity in the Textile Value Chain

fact_notes: 背景となる考え方は添付の資料で確認。本文と練習問題は新規制作。例示した人物・学校・活動は架空の説明用設定。

sentences.en: A student receives a new winter coat and wonders what to do with the older coat that still fits well.
sentences.ja: 生徒は新しい冬のコートを受け取り、まだ着られる古いコートをどうするか考えます。

sentences.en: Throwing it away would be simple, but the coat still contains materials and work that have value.
sentences.ja: 捨てるのは簡単ですが、コートには価値ある素材と労働が含まれています。

sentences.en: However, giving unwanted clothing to another person is not automatically a solution to every environmental problem.
sentences.ja: しかし不要な服を他人に渡すことが、すべての環境問題の解決に自動的につながるわけではありません。

sentences.en: UNEP has examined ways to improve sustainability and circularity throughout the textile value chain.
sentences.ja: UNEPは繊維製品の一連の流れ全体で持続可能性と循環性を高める方法を検討しています。

sentences.en: A product's environmental impact can involve the materials used, the way it is manufactured, and what happens after use.
sentences.ja: 製品の環境影響には素材、製造方法、使用後の行方が関わり得ます。

sentences.en: A responsible choice considers the entire journey of clothing instead of looking only at the moment it is discarded.
sentences.ja: 責任ある選択は廃棄の瞬間だけでなく衣服の全体の流れを考えます。

sentences.en: The student considers repairing a damaged button before offering the old coat to someone else.
sentences.ja: 生徒は古いコートを他人に渡す前に壊れたボタンを直すことを考えます。

sentences.en: For example, a small repair may extend the useful life of an item that would otherwise remain unused.
sentences.ja: 例えば小さな修理が、さもなければ使われない品物の寿命を延ばすかもしれません。

sentences.en: A community exchange event can allow families to find clothing that suits their needs without purchasing new products.
sentences.ja: 地域の交換会では家族が新しい製品を買わずに必要に合う服を見つけられます。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, an exchange works best when the clothes are clean, safe, and appropriate for the people receiving them.
sentences.ja: それでも交換は服が清潔で安全、受け取る人に適しているときに最も機能します。

sentences.en: Simply moving an unusable item from one household to another does not necessarily reduce waste.
sentences.ja: 使えない品物をある家庭から別の家庭へ移すだけでは廃棄物が必ず減るとは限りません。

sentences.en: Quality and actual demand are as important as the number of items collected.
sentences.ja: 集めた数と同様に品質と実際の需要が重要です。

sentences.en: A local organization plans to collect coats and send them to a community with colder winters.
sentences.ja: 地元団体がコートを集め、冬が寒い地域へ送る計画を立てます。

sentences.en: In addition, volunteers ask the receiving community which sizes, materials, and types of clothing are actually needed.
sentences.ja: さらにボランティアは受け入れ地域に必要なサイズ、素材、種類を尋ねます。

sentences.en: Transporting large quantities of unwanted clothing can create costs and may leave recipients with items they cannot use.
sentences.ja: 大量の不要服の輸送には費用がかかり、使えない品物を受け手に残すかもしれません。

sentences.en: The organizers therefore choose to send only suitable items and consider local exchange before international transport.
sentences.ja: 主催者は適切な品だけ送り、海外輸送の前に地元での交換を考えます。

sentences.en: This approach respects the needs of people receiving donations rather than treating them as a place for unwanted goods.
sentences.ja: この方法は受け入れ先を不要品の置き場とせず、必要を尊重します。

sentences.en: A good donation depends on listening as well as giving.
sentences.ja: よい寄付には与えるだけでなく聞くことも必要です。

sentences.en: The school environmental club compares ways to extend the life of clothing without inventing exact savings figures.
sentences.ja: 学校の環境クラブは正確な節約数値を作り上げず、服の寿命を延ばす方法を比較します。

sentences.en: They examine repair, reuse, responsible donation, and the option of buying fewer new items.
sentences.ja: 修理、再利用、責任ある寄付、新しい服の購入を減らす選択を検討します。

sentences.en: Students notice that the best approach depends on the condition of a garment and the needs of its possible user.
sentences.ja: 生徒は最善の方法は衣服の状態と次の利用者の必要によると気づきます。

sentences.en: A strong project avoids claiming that every donated item has the same environmental benefit.
sentences.ja: よい活動は寄付したすべての品が同じ環境利益を持つと主張しません。

sentences.en: Keeping clothes useful for longer requires attention to quality, demand, and the decisions people make before buying.
sentences.ja: 服を長く役立てるには品質、需要、購入前の判断に注意が必要です。

questions.prompt: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Responsible clothing reuse requires quality, demand, and attention to the full product journey.
Every donated garment is equally useful.
Only new clothing should be worn.
questions.explanation_ja: 衣服再利用には品質・需要・全体の流れが重要です。

questions.prompt: What does the student consider repairing?
options: A damaged button on the coat.
questions.explanation_ja: ボタンの修理を考えます。

options: Unusable clothing may simply become a problem for another person.
questions.explanation_ja: 使えない服は負担を移すだけになるためです。

questions.prompt: What can a community exchange offer?
options: Clothing that meets people's needs without a new purchase.
questions.explanation_ja: 地域での再利用機会です。

questions.prompt: What do volunteers ask receiving communities?
options: Which sizes and clothing types they need.
questions.explanation_ja: 受け手のサイズや需要を確かめます。

questions.prompt: Why might large clothing shipments cause problems?
options: They involve transport costs and unwanted items may remain.
questions.explanation_ja: 輸送費と需要不一致が問題です。

options: People's actual need or desire for goods.

questions.prompt: What options does the environmental club compare?
options: Repair, reuse, responsible donation, and reduced purchasing.
questions.explanation_ja: 複数の選択肢を比較します。

questions.prompt: Why does the class avoid exact claims about savings?
options: Environmental effects depend on circumstances not fully measured.
questions.explanation_ja: 条件による違いを測定していないためです。

options: Keeping goods useful requires thoughtful decisions before and after purchase.
Every donation must cross a border.
questions.explanation_ja: 購入前後の判断の重要性で締めます。
